title: Meta Eyes International Expansion for AI Data Centers Following Wave of Local Voter Rejections

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The president of Meta stated that the company is beginning to search for international locations to house its artificial intelligence infrastructure after a series of electoral setbacks for the data center industry. Residents in 10 states voted for restrictions on new facilities in 40 of 41 local ballot measures on Tuesday, indicating a sharp rise in public opposition based on environmental and electricity cost concerns. Dina Powell McCormick noted that while Meta is focusing on expanding existing sites, securing new land in the U.S. has become very challenging, a sentiment mirrored by Anthropic, which recently warned that local moratoriums could threaten future compute availability.

This regulatory friction may leave the U.S. short of projected capacity by 2027. Investor Brad Gerstner predicts that at least 10 to 15 GW of the expected 43 GW of new capacity may not come online due to the victory of candidates who campaigned on restricting the buildout. In Texas, new permits for the power plants required to run these facilities could be paused until mid-2027, which SemiAnalysis warns could leave already funded project shells halfway built but without the electricity needed to operate.

selectedTweets.bestBit: we could see at least 10 to 15 gigawatts of the expected build not come online
selectedTweets.text:
Brad Gerstner says at least 10 to 15 gigawatts of the expected 2027 AI build may not come online after the blue wave, against a consensus 43 gigawatts next year versus about 38 built to date

“Well, I would say not specifically on the gigawatts in Texas, but what I said at the All-In Summit: the consensus forecast, which we’ll call the SemiAnalysis Dylan Patel forecast for next year, is a total of 43 gigawatts coming online in 2027."

"Now, just to put that in perspective, the total gigawatts online at the end of ‘26, the cumulative in the United States, is about 38. So the consensus forecast is we’re going to bring online more next year than all of the compute that we’ve built to date."

"I said on stage, and it got a lot of blowback on Twitter at the time, that we may end up bringing half of that online in 2027. And part of what I was concerned about was the growing backlash, even from guys like Greg Abbott."

"But now with this blue wave, I think it’ll slow it down even more. So I think we could see at least 10 to 15 gigawatts of the expected build not come online, which, you know, that’s why I think it’s going to be really challenging for the AI infra trade."

"We have the dollars to pay for it. But imagine what we’re going to hear, Chamath, for the next two weeks out of the governors, out of Speaker Hakeem Jeffries or Leader Schumer. They ran on slowing down AI. That was their principal agenda.”
selectedTweets.displayQuote: we could see at least 10 to 15 gigawatts of the expected build not come online

selectedTweets.bestBit: the pause on approving new air pollution permits could be extended from, today, the expectation is about December, into the middle of next year
selectedTweets.text:
SemiAnalysis says the permit pause could run to mid-2027, under the Texas Democrats’ plan, and leave funded data center shells without power

Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros: “And as we’ve said to our clients over the last few weeks and few months, because some projects that are under construction today where you see the shell being built that are already funded. Right?"

"So some of them have raised billions, if not tens of billions of dollars to fund the DC, don’t have the final air pollution permit yet, because historically, timelines are fairly short, and so you could sort of get away with this."

"But I think in other states, stuff takes longer to get approved, and so it does not make sense to have this sort of more aggressive construction strategy. And so there’s a risk, as Maya was saying earlier, that if you followed what the Democrats are proposing in Texas, the pause could be extended until new laws are sort of approved."

"That could extend towards perhaps mid-2027, and then the pause on approving new air pollution permits could be extended from, today, the expectation is about December, into the middle of next year. And as you don’t have this final approval, you’re not allowed to actually build the power plant. The data center, you can, and that’s gonna continue. But the power plants, you won’t."

"And so you could actually see a bunch of shells in this scenario that are halfway built or mostly built but don’t have the electricity to run because they were not able to get the permit effectively.”
